parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Good morning. My name is Susan Mossman. As well as being a part-time lecturer on the University’s Museum Science degree, I’m also curator of a new exhibition opening at the Bidmouth Museum called Plasticity. This traces the history of plastics and ways they are being developed and used today. The first type of plastic was originally developed in response to a call from the makers of sports equipment. Animal derived materials were becoming extremely expensive, so manufacturers launched a competition to find an alternative to ivory for making pool and billiard balls. Although various forms of plastic were developed, none of them were good enough to win the competition. But the inventors knew they were on to a good thing and started researching a variety of different substances, partly based on organic material, what we call semi-synthetics. One of the early semi-synthetic materials produced was the first commercially produced celluloid or plastic film, which was made by dissolving cotton in a strong acid, such as nitric acid. Unfortunately, this had a tendency to explode, so technicians had to be very careful with it.

They also experimented with making plastics out of products derived from milk, but this didn’t really work, and efforts were therefore concentrated on other organic material. One of the first uses of plastic was in the production of artificial fabric, and the earliest successful one was a substitute for silk. This was obviously a very expensive fiber, so artificial alternatives were thought to be worth investing in. The next significant breakthrough came in 1907 with the invention of Bakelite. This was the first entirely synthetic plastic made in a laboratory. It was invented by Hendrik Baekeland, a chemist, who had made a fortune from producing paper used in photographic processes. Bakelite is a pretty unusual type of plastic, because it actually gets hard when it’s heated, whereas most other plastic becomes more malleable when hot.

That is, they become more plastic, which is of course where the name for the category of materials comes from. So, strictly speaking, Bakelite isn’t a plastic at all.

But now let’s look at the exhibition itself. In it, we show a variety of semi-synthetic and totally synthetic plastics, some of them dating back 100 years. Some of the older plastics on display are unstable. This means that when they are in the process of degrading, they may produce gases which are acidic, and which can cause neighboring objects in the display to disintegrate. We had to be very careful with these displays, because there is one thing which causes plastic objects to degrade or break down, and that is light.

So, we’ve had to think of ways to get around this problem when setting up the objects on display. We have about 850 objects in the exhibition. One of our most interesting is a magnificent chandelier, a lamp designed to hang in the center of the ceiling of a big hall. It’s only when you look carefully that you can see this is a wonderful example of recycling. It’s made entirely of pens, ones which we use and throw away every day. A second exhibit, which is drawing a lot of attention, is a car made entirely from plastic, which is now in small scale production in Japan.

analyses.content: 录音中提到第一种商业化生产的 celluloid（赛璐珞）是通过溶解 cotton（棉花）制成的，对应填空中的 used ______。
One of the early semi-synthetic materials produced was the first commercially produced celluloid or plastic film, which was made by dissolving cotton in a strong acid, such as nitric acid.
你可能会听到后面的 acid（酸），但那是用来溶解棉花的溶剂，不是原材料本身。
They also experimented with making plastics out of products derived from milk, but this didn’t really work, and efforts were therefore concentrated on other organic material.
虽然这句话紧接着说了 didn’t really work（没成功），但这正好对应题干的 unsuccessful，所以答案就是 milk。
听到 experimented with（尝试实验）时注意，录音说他们尝试用源自 milk（牛奶）的产品制作塑料，对应题干 from ______ products。
One of the first uses of plastic was in the production of artificial fabric, and the earliest successful one was a substitute for silk.
题目问的是“人造的什么”，填空位置在 artificial 后面，虽然它是丝绸的替代品，但在英语表达中 artificial silk（人造丝）指代的就是这种新织物。
录音提到最早成功的 artificial fabric（人造织物）是一种 silk（丝绸）的替代品（substitute）。
The next significant breakthrough came in 1907 with the invention of Bakelite. This was the first entirely synthetic plastic made in a laboratory.
听到 1907 和 Bakelite 时定位，录音明确说这是第一种完全在 laboratory（实验室）里制造的合成塑料。
It was invented by Hendrik Baekeland, a chemist, who had made a fortune from producing paper used in photographic processes.
不要填 inventor，虽然他是发明者，但题目空格前有不定冠词 a，且录音中特定的职业身份词是 chemist。
听到发明者名字 Hendrik Baekeland 前，录音先介绍了他是一位 chemist（化学家），对应题干 invented by a...。
Bakelite is a pretty unusual type of plastic, because it actually gets hard when it’s heated, whereas most other plastic becomes more malleable when hot.
千万别填 malleable（可塑的/易变形的），录音说的是 whereas most other plastic becomes more malleable（然而大多数其他塑料会变软），这是用来做对比的干扰项。
录音中出现转折 actually，强调这种塑料很特别，因为它受热时会变 hard（硬）。
This means that when they are in the process of degrading, they may produce gases which are acidic, and which can cause neighboring objects in the display to disintegrate.
话题转换到 Exhibition（展览），录音说旧塑料在降解过程中会产生酸性的 gases（气体），对应题干 release acidic...。
We had to be very careful with these displays, because there is one thing which causes plastic objects to degrade or break down, and that is light.
录音强调有一样东西会导致塑料降解（degrade），那就是 light（光）。
It’s only when you look carefully that you can see this is a wonderful example of recycling. It’s made entirely of pens, ones which we use and throw away every day.
题目问的是 recycled（回收利用的）什么东西，不要填 plastic，虽然是塑料做的，但具体物品是 pens。
听到 chandelier（吊灯）后，仔细听它的材料，录音说是完全由我们每天扔掉的 pens（钢笔/圆珠笔）制成的。
A second exhibit, which is drawing a lot of attention, is a car made entirely from plastic, which is now in small scale production in Japan.
录音提到第二个吸引注意力的展品是一辆完全由塑料制成的 car（汽车），并且是在日本生产的。
